\chapter{Shouts in the Street}

\hlchaptermodality{299}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say who shouted, who stopped whom, and that everyone was safe.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ચીસ} (cīs)}{ચીસ (cīs)}]{\gu{ચીસ} (cīs) — a scream}

\label{lesson:GU-C299-cis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for consolation, then the Gujarati for to bear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ચીસ}}
\textbf{\gu{ચીસ}} — \emph{cīs} — \textquotedblleft{}a scream\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{અચાનક} \gu{મીરાના} \gu{મોઢામાંથી} \gu{ચીસ} \gu{નીકળી} \gu{ગઈ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{acānak Mīrānā moḍhāmā̃thī cīs nīkḷī gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Suddenly a scream broke from Mira.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ચીસ}} (\emph{cīs}) comes from \emph{*cīssa}, \textquotedblleft{}a sharp pain\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs, and CDIAL lists Gujarati \emph{cīs}, \textquotedblleft{}a scream\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4847): the cry that pain draws out. A scream \textbf{\gu{નીકળે} \gu{છે}}, comes out of you: \textbf{\gu{ચીસ} \gu{નીકળી} \gu{ગઈ}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cīs}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cīs}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{acānak Mīrānā moḍhāmā̃thī cīs nīkḷī gaī.} — Suddenly a scream broke from Mira.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for consolation, then the Gujarati for to bear, then say \emph{cīs} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ચીસ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A scream\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બૂમ} (būm)}{બૂમ (būm)}]{\gu{બૂમ} (būm) — a shout}

\label{lesson:GU-C299-bum}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to bear, then the Gujarati for a scream.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બૂમ}}
\textbf{\gu{બૂમ}} — \emph{būm} — \textquotedblleft{}a shout\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{લોકોએ} \gu{બૂમો} \gu{મારી} \gu{અને} \gu{ચોર} \gu{નાસી} \gu{ગયો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lokoe būmo mārī ane cor nāsī gayo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People shouted and the thief ran off.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બૂમ}} (\emph{būm}) No dictionary we use records an older form, so its history is not settled. A shout is given with \textbf{\gu{મારવું}}: \textbf{\gu{બૂમ} \gu{મારી}}, called out loudly.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{būm}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{būm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lokoe būmo mārī ane cor nāsī gayo.} — People shouted and the thief ran off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to bear, then the Gujarati for a scream, then say \emph{būm} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{બૂમ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A shout\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{રોકવું} (rokvũ)}{રોકવું (rokvũ)}]{\gu{રોકવું} (rokvũ) — to bring to a stop}

\label{lesson:GU-C299-rokvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a scream, then the Gujarati for a shout.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{રોકવું}}
\textbf{\gu{રોકવું}} — \emph{rokvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to bring to a stop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{સિપાઈએ} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{રોકી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sipāīe gāḍī rokī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The constable stopped the car.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{રોકી}, \emph{teṇe gāḍī rokī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{રોકવું}} (\emph{rokvũ}) comes from \emph{*rōkk}, \textquotedblleft{}stop\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs, and CDIAL lists the Gujarati verb (CDIAL 10827). It is the doing partner of \textbf{\gu{રોકાવું}}, to stay on: \textbf{\gu{સિપાઈએ} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{રોકી}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rokvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rokvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sipāīe gāḍī rokī.} — The constable stopped the car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a scream, then the Gujarati for a shout, then say \emph{rokvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{અટકાવવું} (aṭkāvvũ)}{અટકાવવું (aṭkāvvũ)}]{\gu{અટકાવવું} (aṭkāvvũ) — to hold back; to prevent}

\label{lesson:GU-C299-atkavvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a shout, then the Gujarati for to bring to a stop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{અટકાવવું}}
\textbf{\gu{અટકાવવું}} — \emph{aṭkāvvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold back; to prevent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મીરાએ} \gu{હાથ} \gu{પકડીને} \gu{બાળકને} \gu{અટકાવ્યું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mīrāe hāth pakḍīne bāḷakne aṭkāvyũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mira took the child's hand and held him back.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{બાળકને} \gu{અટકાવ્યું}, \emph{teṇe bāḷakne aṭkāvyũ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{અટકાવવું}} (\emph{aṭkāvvũ}) is the causative of \textbf{\gu{અટકવું}}, to stop, from \emph{*aṭṭakk}, \textquotedblleft{}obstruct, stop\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 182): to make someone stop before something happens.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭkāvvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Mīrāe hāth pakḍīne bāḷakne aṭkāvyũ.} — Mira took the child's hand and held him back.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a shout, then the Gujarati for to bring to a stop, then say \emph{aṭkāvvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{સલામત} (salāmat)}{સલામત (salāmat)}]{\gu{સલામત} (salāmat) — safe}

\label{lesson:GU-C299-salamat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to bring to a stop, then the Gujarati for to hold back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{સલામત}}
\textbf{\gu{સલામત}} — \emph{salāmat} — \textquotedblleft{}safe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{છેવટે} \gu{બધા} \gu{સલામત} \gu{હતા}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chevṭe badhā salāmat hatā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end everyone was safe.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{સલામત}} (\emph{salāmat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{salāma}, \textquotedblleft{}safety, soundness\textquotedblright{}. It describes people and things out of danger: \textbf{\gu{બધા} \gu{સલામત} \gu{છે}}, everyone is safe.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{salāmat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{salāmat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chevṭe badhā salāmat hatā.} — In the end everyone was safe.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to bring to a stop, then the Gujarati for to hold back, then say \emph{salāmat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
